requirements.requirement: The system must map backend malpractice data to a UI status of 'clean' when case_count is 0 or explicitly marked as no incidents.
The system must map backend malpractice data to a UI status of 'flagged' when case_count is greater than 0 or an incident exists.
The system must map backend malpractice data to a UI status of 'unknown' when malpractice data is null, missing, or incomplete.
The system must display only neutral signal language when presenting malpractice status, avoiding any implication of intent or wrongdoing.
The system must not render prohibited terms including 'fraud', 'misconduct', or synonyms in any malpractice-related UI text.
The system must calculate score_contribution for malpractice using the backend-provided weight or value without modification.
The system must format score_contribution into a human-readable string consistent with other provider score components.
The system must ensure that malpractice status labels are deterministic and produce the same output for identical backend inputs.
The system must gracefully fallback to 'unknown' status when backend data contains invalid values (e.g., negative case_count).
The system must omit optional fields such as case_count and last_incident_date from display logic when they are null without causing rendering errors.
The system must ensure that all generated malpractice display text is compatible with the MessageBubble.tsx markdown-safe rendering pipeline.
The system must enforce a consistent mapping between status values and display labels (e.g., 'clean' -> 'No reported malpractice signals').
The system must ensure that no backend raw text fields are directly rendered without passing through the neutral-language transformation layer.
The system must log a non-blocking warning when malpractice data is missing or malformed while still rendering a valid UI state.
